title: Notation reference card
subject: Mathematics
unit: Summer 1: Geometric notation and constructions; geometric reasoning
source: Seeded from mathematics/y7 lesson 52 (Notation reference card (printable, in the pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 52: Geometric notation: points, lines and line segments. To understand how geometric notation describes points, lines, line segments and shapes precisely

questions.q: Triangle ABC has AB = AC. How do we show this on a diagram, and what type of triangle is it?
questions.a: One dash on AB and one dash on AC; isosceles
questions.model: Equal sides get the same number of dashes: one dash on AB, one on AC. Two equal sides make the triangle isosceles.

questions.q: Name all four sides of quadrilateral KLMN.
Write in notation: line segment EF is parallel to line segment GH.
How many diagonals does pentagon ABCDE have? Name them.
Parallelogram ABCD is labelled in order. (a) Which side is parallel to AB? (b) Which side is equal to AD? (c) Name both diagonals. (d) Write one statement using ∥.
questions.a: (a) DC (b) BC (c) AC and BD (d) AD ∥ BC (or AB ∥ DC)
questions.model: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel and equal: AB with DC, AD with BC. Diagonals join opposite corners: A to C and B to D.

questions.q: A hexagon has vertices A to F. How many diagonals does it have? Explain a quick way to count them.
questions.a: 9: from each of 6 vertices there are 3 diagonals (not to itself or its 2 neighbours); 6 × 3 = 18 counts each one twice, so 9

questions.q: Find a rule for the number of diagonals of a polygon with n sides. Test it on an octagon.
Rectangle PQRS: name the side parallel to QR.
Big question: why do mathematicians label shapes with letters?
questions.a: So everyone means exactly the same point, line or angle; words alone can be misunderstood.
